newsitem.title: USA: GM shares start new year on strong note.
newsitem.headline: GM shares start new year on strong note.

text.p: Shares in General Motors Corp began the new year on a strong note Thursday with investors anticipating better performance and a divestiture of Hughes Electronics Corp, analysts said.
GM shares were up 2-3/4 at 58-1/2 in composite trading.
Lehman Brothers auto analyst Joseph Phillippi said he thought GM's stock was bouncing back Thursday from year-end selling by investment portfolio managers last week.

"A lot of portfolio managers aggressively sold the stock in the last week or so of December," Phillippi said. "A lot of them still like the (GM) story, so some may well have come back at the start of the new year."
Phillippi said GM is expected to improve its earnings in 1997 over 1996, a year marred by costly labor disputes. GM is expected to reap benefits from a host of new product offerings in 1997, he said.

Smith Barney auto analyst David Garrity noted that a strong monthly report from the National Association of Purchasing Management and continued anticipation of a multibillion-dollar spin-off or sale of GM's Hughes Electronics Corp subsidiary also may have contributed to the rise in GM stock. GM Class H shares, which are tied to Hughes' performance, were up 1-5/8 to 57-7/8 in composite trading.

GM has repeatedly declined to comment on specific plans for Hughes, but said in documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission in November 1996 that the subsidiary wants to "strengthen its leadership position through acquisitions, consolidations, realignments and divestitures."

Garrity also noted that some investors may be buying in anticipation of the start of next week's North American International Auto Show, where automakers will unveil significant new products. Chrysler Corp shares were up 1-1/8 to 34-1/8, and Ford Motor Co shares were up 1/8 to 32.
